newsitem.title: UK: Sterling firm in Europe, cable holds above $1.64.
newsitem.headline: Sterling firm in Europe, cable holds above $1.64.

text.p: Sterling was firm around 3.03 marks and $1.64 in Europe, recovering after a brief dip though well buoyed by rate-rise expectations, said traders.
Sterling recovered after easing a touch as data showed the UK's Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) falling slightly in July to 53.4 from a revised 53.5 in June.
"Sterling dipped a bit, but then recovered. The PMI had only a limited effect on the market," said Duncan Frost from Bank Brussels Lambert (BBL) sales department.
But the survey, which showed Britain's manufacturing sector growing for the fourteenth month in succession, showed output holding up well despite the impact of the strong pound.
Marginally bearish for sterling was a large decline in the prices component of the index to 38.3 from June's 43.6 - to its lowest level since the survey began.

"The survey...offers hope that inflation will remain under control despite strong growth at home. If so, expectations of some analysts for base rates to go up to 8 percent may well prove too bearish," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy.
At 1000 GMT, sterling/mark stood at 3.0270/80 against 3.0130/40 in late Europe on Thursday.
Cable was trading at $1.6420/30 against $1.6404/14 in late Europe on Thursday.
But some in the market are banking on higher interest rates to quash domestic demand.
"While we are seeing problems with exports...sterling is still supported by a dynamic economy," said Claudio Demolli, foreign exchange analyst at Merrill Lynch.
Gains the dollar made against the mark also gave sterling a boost against the German currency on Friday. At 1015 GMT, dollar/mark was at 1.8454/59 compared with 1.8395/05 late in Europe on Thursday.
Traders said sterling was also trying to find a base against the mark and dollar on Friday after its exhausting collapse and recovery earlier this week.
The pound slid from a high of 3.0627 marks on Monday to a low of 2.9735 marks on Tuesday and was back above 3.03 marks on Friday.

"The pound is taking a bit of a breather, and trying to find a new base against the dollar and Europe. It could go higher, but in the meantime it remains well underpinned," said a trader at a UK merchant bank.

Traders said the pound was still drawing strength after UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said in an interview on Thursday he had no plans for a special autumn budget to brake consumer spending and hinted at no intervention on markets to stem the pound's gains.
The pound could also find fresh direction from July U.S. jobs data due later on Friday, said traders.
